# ezghcloud_route_table (Resource)

Manage a VPC route table and its complete set of routes. A subnet uses the table once its `route_table_id` names it. Do not manage the same table's routes with another resource or tool.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Outbound IPv4 for a private subnet: the NAT gateway sits in a public subnet, and the private
# subnet uses a route table whose default route targets it.
resource "ezghcloud_nat_gateway" "example" {
  project_id = ezghcloud_project.example.id
  name       = "egress"
  vpc_id     = ezghcloud_vpc.example.id
  subnet_id  = ezghcloud_subnet.public.id
}

resource "ezghcloud_route_table" "private" {
  project_id = ezghcloud_project.example.id
  vpc_id     = ezghcloud_vpc.example.id
  name       = "private"

  routes = [{
    destination = "0.0.0.0/0"
    target_type = "natGateway"
    target_id   = ezghcloud_nat_gateway.example.id
  }]
}

resource "ezghcloud_subnet" "private" {
  project_id     = ezghcloud_project.example.id
  vpc_id         = ezghcloud_vpc.example.id
  name           = "private"
  ipv4_cidr      = "10.0.2.0/24"
  route_table_id = ezghcloud_route_table.private.id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Resource name.
- `project_id` (String) Project owning this resource.
- `vpc_id` (String) VPC (vpc_) the table belongs to. Changing it replaces the table.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Optional resource description; null clears it.
- `routes` (Attributes Set) Complete set of the table's routes, one per destination. Omitted or [] means no routes. The VPC's local routes are always present and are not listed. A route whose target is deleted, detached or not yet active stays configured and carries no traffic until the target is back. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes))
- `tags` (Map of String) Customer resource tags.

### Read-Only

- `etag` (String) Version of the route set, used for conditional route replacement.
- `id` (String) Canonical prefixed resource ID (rtb_).
- `main` (Boolean) Whether this is the VPC's main table, used by every subnet without a table of its own. A created table never is; an imported main table can't be destroyed (it is deleted with its VPC).
- `organization_id` (String) Organization owning this resource.
- `resource_name` (String) IAM resource name.

<a id="nestedatt--routes"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes`

Required:

- `destination` (String) Canonical destination CIDR, IPv4 or IPv6, such as 0.0.0.0/0.
- `target_id` (String) The target's ID: the VPC's attached Network Gateway (ngw_), a private network interface in the VPC (eni_) or a NAT gateway of the VPC (nat_).
- `target_type` (String) networkGateway, networkInterface or natGateway.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Replace identifiers with values from your organization.
terraform import ezghcloud_route_table.example 'ORGANIZATION_ID/PROJECT_ID/RESOURCE_ID'
```
